minutes.headline: Committee sent policy 1202 on school facility use back to subcommittee and approved the FY23 capital plan.
minutes.summary: The committee heard public comment on the facility-use policy, approved minutes and a large salary transfer, and sent the facility-use policy back to the policy subcommittee. It approved the FY23 capital submission, gave an informal no-objection to a new town hall on school land, and discussed bus expansion and a hybrid meeting model.

budget_items.topic: Primary school air conditioning capital request
budget_items.what_was_said: Engineer estimate with new electrical service versus a lower estimate if existing panels can be used; classroom wings cost less than the cafeteria and music room. Recommended submitting the lower figure with contingency.

budget_items.topic: One ton dump truck with plow
budget_items.what_was_said: Replacement of a 2008 truck requested; adding a sander would cost more and the DPW already sands school grounds.
Replace a 2000 mower with a smaller zero-turn unit, price still a planning estimate.
Youth soccer association pays roughly this for hourly use of grass fields; concern about charging kids while adults pay nothing.
Each added bus costs a set annual amount in FY22 and likely more, with two buses costing roughly double; not included in contract negotiation models.

budget_items.topic: Possible bus fee for riders under a mile and a half
budget_items.what_was_said: Committee discussed surveying parents and other districts about a fee to offset transporting all students.
Rec department may charge a small fee to cover registration platform overhead, not yet decided.
Finance committee report that free cash is coming in higher than anticipated but not yet certified.

transfers.description: Salary and wages transfers among school line items after fall hiring, including reserve, kindergarten, psychologist moved to grant, paraprofessional lines

decisions.decision: First read of facility-use policy 1202 declared null and void and returned to the policy subcommittee to incorporate the park commission's comments and adult program question.
Lifelong adult learning program: no action; staff to talk with the recreation director and community schools director about where programs belong.
Capital submission to go to the town by the October 14 deadline with the lower air conditioning figure, to be revised later if the engineers disagree.
Administration will gather ridership, bus cost, other-district fee data; any decision to add buses is needed by the January 5 meeting.
Add setting committee goals and a follow-up on the hybrid meeting model to future topics.

what_happened.line: The School Committee sent first reading of facility-use policy 1202 back to the policy subcommittee to take in the park commission's comments and an adult-program question.
It accepted the FY23 capital plan 5-0, with the air conditioning request at the lower figure, to go to the town by the October 14 deadline.
It approved a salary and wages line item transfer 5-0 by roll call.
It authorized a relay of its lack of objection to a town hall on school property, 5-0, and waived the first reading of policy 5204.
It voted 5-0 to meet in person the first Wednesday and on Zoom the third Wednesday; administration is to gather bus data before a January 5 decision.

why_it_matters: The capital plan sets what school-side projects, such as primary school air conditioning, go to the town as requests, and those requests compete for town funding.
Any added buses or a fee for short-distance riders would reach families and the school budget, and a decision is due by January 5.
Facility-use rules decide who can use school fields and rooms, and what youth sports groups and adult programs are charged.
watch_next: The January 5 meeting, by which a decision on adding buses is needed.
